q: Chennai Metro Rail Limited (CMRL) was incorporated as a special purpose vehicle in the year:
e: Chennai Metro Rail Limited was incorporated in 2007 as a special purpose vehicle to implement the Chennai Metro Rail project for the city of Chennai.

q: The National Academy of Indian Railways (NAIR) at Vadodara is headed by an officer holding the designation of:
e: The National Academy of Indian Railways at Vadodara, the apex training academy for railway officers, is headed by an officer holding the designation of Director General.

q: The headquarters of the Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA) is located at:
e: The headquarters of the Rail Land Development Authority, which develops vacant railway land and air space for commercial use, is located at New Delhi.

q: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor is being implemented by DFCCIL with loan assistance mainly from the:
e: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor is being implemented by DFCCIL mainly with loan assistance from the Japan International Cooperation Agency, while the Eastern Corridor drew World Bank support.

q: The Carriage Repair Workshop at Hubballi is located in which State?
e: The Carriage Repair Workshop at Hubballi, which overhauls passenger coaches of South Western Railway, is located in the State of Karnataka.

q: The Zonal Railway Training Institute at Alipurduar Junction functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Zonal Railway Training Institute at Alipurduar Junction, training staff of the Alipurduar division area, functions under Northeast Frontier Railway.

q: The Zonal Railway Training Institute at Ponmalai (Golden Rock), Tiruchirappalli, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Zonal Railway Training Institute at Ponmalai, known as Golden Rock, at Tiruchirappalli functions under Southern Railway, whose headquarters is at Chennai.

q: The Rail Wheel Factory at Bengaluru was originally set up under the name:
e: The Rail Wheel Factory at Bengaluru, which manufactures wheels and axles for Indian Railways, was originally set up under the name Wheel and Axle Plant.

q: Western Railway was formed in the year:
e: Western Railway was formed in 1951 by merging the Bombay, Baroda and Central India Railway with other western region railways, with headquarters at Churchgate, Mumbai.

q: The Modern Coach Factory of Indian Railways is situated at which place in the Raebareli district of Uttar Pradesh?
e: The Modern Coach Factory of Indian Railways is situated at Lalganj in the Raebareli district of Uttar Pradesh, where it builds modern LHB coaches.

q: The Diesel Loco Shed at Visakhapatnam, the largest diesel locomotive shed of Indian Railways, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Visakhapatnam Diesel Loco Shed now functions under the Visakhapatnam division of the South Coast Railway, the zone operational from 1 June 2026; it earlier worked under East Coast Railway through the Waltair division.

q: The Electric Loco Shed at Jhansi functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Electric Loco Shed at Jhansi, which maintains electric locomotives of the Jhansi division, functions under North Central Railway, headquartered at Prayagraj.

q: The headquarters office of South Eastern Railway is located at which locality of Kolkata?
e: The headquarters office of South Eastern Railway is located at Garden Reach in Kolkata, the historic garden house complex on the bank of the Hooghly.

q: The headquarters office of Northern Railway at New Delhi is housed in the historic building known as:
e: The headquarters office of Northern Railway at New Delhi is housed in Baroda House, the historic building near India Gate that was earlier the Delhi residence of the Maharaja of Baroda.

q: In Indian Railways, 'NHSRCL' stands for:

options.A: National High Speed Railway Company Limited
options.B: National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited
options.C: National Highway Speed Rail Corporation Limited
options.D: New High Speed Rail Corporation Limited

e: NHSRCL stands for National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited, the special purpose vehicle implementing the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high speed rail corridor.

q: 'KRCL', the company that built and operates the Konkan Railway, stands for:
e: KRCL stands for Konkan Railway Corporation Limited, the company that built and operates the Konkan Railway between Roha and Thokur along the west coast.

q: 'NAIR', the apex training academy of Indian Railways at Vadodara, stands for:
e: NAIR stands for National Academy of Indian Railways, the apex training academy at Vadodara that trains probationary and serving officers of all railway services.

q: 'RDSO', the research and standards organisation of Indian Railways at Lucknow, stands for:
e: RDSO stands for Research Designs and Standards Organisation, the research and standards organisation of Indian Railways headquartered at Lucknow.

q: 'CAMTECH', the maintenance technology centre of Indian Railways at Gwalior, stands for:
e: CAMTECH stands for Centre for Advanced Maintenance Technology, the Railway Board centre at Gwalior that develops improved maintenance practices for rolling stock and assets.

q: In railway security, 'RPSF' stands for:
e: In railway security, RPSF stands for Railway Protection Special Force, the armed battalion force of the RPF deployed for sensitive and emergency duties.

q: The unified Group 'A' service of Indian Railways denoted by 'IRMS' stands for:
e: IRMS stands for Indian Railway Management Service, the unified Group A service created by merging the eight organised Group A services of Indian Railways.

q: 'IRWO', the welfare organisation that builds housing colonies for railway employees, stands for:
e: IRWO stands for Indian Railway Welfare Organisation, the welfare body that builds residential housing colonies for serving and retired railway employees.

q: 'REMCL', the joint venture company for procurement of power for Indian Railways, stands for:
e: REMCL stands for Railway Energy Management Company Limited, the joint venture of Indian Railways and RITES for procurement of economical power for the Railways.

q: 'IRSDC', the company set up for redevelopment of railway stations, stands for:

options.A: Indian Railway Stations Development Company Limited
options.B: Indian Railway Stations Development Corporation Limited
options.C: Indian Rail Stations Design Corporation Limited
options.D: Integrated Railway Station Development Corporation Limited

e: IRSDC stands for Indian Railway Stations Development Corporation Limited, the company set up for redevelopment and commercial development of railway stations.

q: 'MRVC', the company implementing suburban railway projects in Mumbai, stands for:
e: MRVC stands for Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Limited, the joint venture implementing suburban railway improvement projects in Mumbai under the Mumbai Urban Transport Project.

q: Who took over as the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Railway Board in September 2024?
e: Satish Kumar, a former General Manager of North Central Railway, took over as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Railway Board in September 2024.

q: The first freight train to reach the Kashmir Valley, in August 2025, arrived at the Anantnag goods shed carrying:
e: The first freight train to reach the Kashmir Valley in August 2025 arrived at the Anantnag goods shed carrying cement, marking the start of rail freight into the Valley.

q: The Agartala-Akhaura cross-border rail link between India and Bangladesh, inaugurated in November 2023, has a total length of about:
e: The Agartala-Akhaura cross-border rail link between India and Bangladesh, inaugurated in November 2023, has a total length of about 12.24 km, split between the two countries.

q: Which type of train service was flagged off for the first time in the Kashmir Valley in February 2024, on the opening of the Banihal-Sangaldan section of the USBRL project?
e: On the opening of the Banihal-Sangaldan section of the USBRL project in February 2024, the first train service flagged off in the Kashmir Valley was an electric train.

q: In July 2025, the Integral Coach Factory, Chennai successfully tested India's first hydrogen-powered:
e: In July 2025 the Integral Coach Factory, Chennai successfully tested India's first hydrogen-powered driving power car, the traction unit of the hydrogen train project.

q: The first section of the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor, dedicated to the nation in December 2020, was the section between:
e: The first section of the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor dedicated to the nation in December 2020 was the section between New Khurja and New Bhaupur in Uttar Pradesh.

q: The redeveloped Ayodhya Dham Junction railway station (Phase-I) was inaugurated by the Prime Minister in:
e: The redeveloped Ayodhya Dham Junction railway station, Phase-I, with its temple-inspired architecture, was inaugurated by the Prime Minister in December 2023.

q: The Charlapalli railway terminal, inaugurated in January 2025, has been developed as the fourth major passenger terminal of which city?
e: The Charlapalli railway terminal, inaugurated in January 2025, has been developed as the fourth major passenger terminal of Hyderabad, after Secunderabad, Hyderabad Deccan and Kacheguda.

q: The first 'Kisan Rail' service of Indian Railways, started in August 2020, was run between Devlali in Maharashtra and:
e: The first Kisan Rail service of Indian Railways, started in August 2020 for carrying perishable farm produce, was run between Devlali in Maharashtra and Danapur in Bihar.

q: The complete 82 km Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut 'Namo Bharat' RRTS corridor was dedicated to the nation in:
e: The complete 82 km Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut Namo Bharat RRTS corridor was dedicated to the nation in February 2026, completing the first RRTS corridor of India end to end.

q: The famous play 'Waiting for Godot', a landmark of the theatre of the absurd, was written by:
e: Waiting for Godot, the landmark play of the theatre of the absurd in which Vladimir and Estragon wait for the unseen Godot, was written by Samuel Beckett.

q: The celebrated modernist poem 'The Waste Land' (1922) was written by:
e: The Waste Land of 1922, the celebrated modernist poem of post-war disillusionment in five sections, was written by T. S. Eliot.

q: The book 'The Prophet' (1923), a collection of poetic essays on life and the human condition, was written by:
e: The Prophet of 1923, a collection of poetic essays on love, freedom, work and other themes of life, was written by the Lebanese-American writer Kahlil Gibran.

q: The novella 'The Metamorphosis', in which the travelling salesman Gregor Samsa wakes up transformed into an insect, was written by:
e: The Metamorphosis, the novella in which the travelling salesman Gregor Samsa wakes up transformed into a huge insect, was written by Franz Kafka.

q: The play 'A Doll's House', famous for its portrayal of Nora Helmer, was written by:
e: A Doll's House, the play famous for its portrayal of Nora Helmer, who finally leaves her husband and home, was written by the Norwegian playwright Henrik Ibsen.

q: The philosophical work 'Meditations', written as the private notebooks of a Roman emperor, was authored by:
e: Meditations, the philosophical work written as the private notebooks of a Roman emperor practising Stoicism, was authored by Marcus Aurelius.

q: The ancient Chinese military treatise 'The Art of War' is traditionally attributed to:
e: The Art of War, the ancient Chinese military treatise on strategy and tactics, is traditionally attributed to the Chinese general and strategist Sun Tzu.

q: The Sanskrit play 'Swapnavasavadatta', centred on King Udayana and Vasavadatta, is attributed to:
e: Swapnavasavadatta, the Sanskrit play centred on King Udayana of Vatsa and his queen Vasavadatta, is attributed to the early dramatist Bhasa.

q: The Sanskrit epic poem 'Kumarasambhava', describing the birth of Kartikeya, was composed by:
e: Kumarasambhava, the Sanskrit epic poem describing the marriage of Shiva and Parvati and the birth of their son Kartikeya, was composed by Kalidasa.

q: The Sanskrit collection of fables and moral tales 'Hitopadesha' is traditionally attributed to:
e: Hitopadesha, the Sanskrit collection of fables and moral tales drawn largely from the Panchatantra, is traditionally attributed to Narayana.

q: The Sanskrit ocean of story, 'Kathasaritsagara', was composed by:
e: Kathasaritsagara, the Sanskrit ocean of story retelling the lost Brihatkatha in verse, was composed by the Kashmiri poet Somadeva.

q: The celebrated Malayalam novel 'Chemmeen', centred on the fishing community of the Kerala coast, was written by:
e: Chemmeen, the celebrated Malayalam novel centred on the fishing community of the Kerala coast and the Karuthamma-Pareekutty story, was written by Thakazhi Sivasankara Pillai.

q: The famous Hindi novel 'Maila Anchal' (1954), a landmark of the regional novel, was written by:
e: Maila Anchal of 1954, the landmark Hindi regional novel set in the Purnia region of Bihar, was written by Phanishwar Nath Renu.

q: The Hindi novel 'Kitne Pakistan', which won the Sahitya Akademi Award, was written by:
e: Kitne Pakistan, the Hindi novel that surveys communal history through a courtroom of historical figures and won the Sahitya Akademi Award, was written by Kamleshwar.

q: The celebrated Urdu novel 'Aag Ka Darya' (River of Fire), spanning over two thousand years of history, was written by:
e: Aag Ka Darya, the celebrated Urdu novel River of Fire spanning over two thousand years of Indian history, was written by Qurratulain Hyder.

q: The dystopian novel 'Nineteen Eighty-Four', which introduced the figure of Big Brother, was written by:
e: George Orwell wrote Nineteen Eighty-Four, the dystopian novel published in 1949 that introduced Big Brother and the totalitarian state of Oceania.

q: The novel 'Sense and Sensibility', the first published novel of its author, was written by:
e: Sense and Sensibility, published in 1811, was Jane Austen's first published novel, preceding Pride and Prejudice and her later works.

q: The Tandon Committee (1974), appointed by the Reserve Bank of India under the chairmanship of Prakash Tandon, framed guidelines mainly relating to:
e: The Tandon Committee of 1974, chaired by Prakash Tandon for the RBI, laid down norms for bank lending for working capital, including inventory norms and the MPBF method.

q: The Whitley Commission (1929), appointed as the Royal Commission on Labour, inquired into the conditions of:
e: The Whitley Commission of 1929 was the Royal Commission on Labour, appointed to inquire into the conditions of labour in India in industry and plantations.

q: The Fraser Commission (1902-03), chaired by Sir Andrew Fraser, was appointed to inquire into the working of the:
e: The Fraser Commission of 1902-03, chaired by Sir Andrew Fraser, inquired into the working of the police in India and recommended reforms in police administration.

q: The Lee Commission (1924), chaired by Lord Lee of Fareham, was the Royal Commission appointed to examine the:
e: The Lee Commission of 1924, chaired by Lord Lee of Fareham, was the Royal Commission on the Superior Civil Services in India and examined their organisation and conditions.

q: The Bhoothalingam Committee (1978) was appointed by the Government of India to study and report on:
e: The Bhoothalingam Committee of 1978 was appointed to study and report on wages, incomes and prices policy, covering the relationship among the three.

q: The Muddiman Committee (1924), officially the Reforms Inquiry Committee, was appointed to investigate the working of:

options.D: Dyarchy under the Government of India Act, 1919

e: The Muddiman Committee of 1924, the Reforms Inquiry Committee, investigated the working of dyarchy introduced in the provinces by the Government of India Act, 1919.

q: The Skeen Committee (1925), also known as the Indian Sandhurst Committee, was appointed to report on:

options.A: The training of Indians for commissioned ranks in the Army
options.B: The expansion of the Indian Navy

e: The Skeen Committee of 1925, called the Indian Sandhurst Committee, reported on training Indians for commissioned ranks in the Army, leading towards an Indian Sandhurst.

q: The Sapru Committee (1945), chaired by Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru, is best known for its report containing:

options.A: A plan for the partition of India
options.B: Constitutional proposals for the future set-up of India
options.C: Proposals for the demarcation of provincial boundaries
options.D: A long-term food policy for India

e: The Sapru Committee of 1945, chaired by Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru, is known for its report containing constitutional proposals for the future set-up of India.

q: The Dhar Commission (1948), chaired by S. K. Dhar, was appointed by the Constituent Assembly to examine the question of:

options.B: The official language of the Union
options.C: The formation of provinces on a linguistic basis

e: The Dhar Commission of 1948, chaired by S. K. Dhar, was appointed by the Constituent Assembly to examine the formation of provinces on a linguistic basis.

q: The Thakkar Commission, chaired by Justice M. P. Thakkar, was appointed to inquire into:

options.A: The excesses committed during the Emergency
options.C: The demolition of the disputed structure at Ayodhya
options.D: The assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi

e: The Thakkar Commission, chaired by Justice M. P. Thakkar, inquired into the assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in 1984 and the security lapses involved.

q: The Kelkar Task Forces of 2002, headed by Vijay Kelkar, were set up to recommend reforms in:

options.D: The disinvestment of public sector undertakings

e: The Kelkar Task Forces of 2002, headed by Vijay Kelkar, were set up to recommend reforms in direct and indirect taxation, leading to proposals for tax simplification.

q: The Parliament of Japan is known as the:
e: The Parliament of Japan is called the National Diet, consisting of the House of Representatives and the House of Councillors.

q: The Sargasso Sea, known for its floating seaweed and the absence of a coastline, is located in the:
e: The Sargasso Sea, noted for floating Sargassum seaweed and having no coastline, lies in the North Atlantic Ocean, bounded only by ocean currents.

q: The International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer is observed every year on:
e: The International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer is observed on 16 September, marking the signing of the Montreal Protocol on that date in 1987.

q: Human Rights Day, marking the adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, is observed every year on:
e: Human Rights Day is observed on 10 December, the date in 1948 when the UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

q: The first peak above 8,000 metres to be climbed, summited in 1950 by a French expedition, was:
e: Annapurna I was the first peak above 8,000 metres to be climbed, summited in 1950 by a French expedition led by Maurice Herzog, before Everest in 1953.

q: Umananda, the small river island at Guwahati also known as Peacock Island, is located in the river:
e: Umananda, also called Peacock Island, is a small river island at Guwahati located in the Brahmaputra river, and is known for its Shiva temple.

q: The Cook Strait separates the North Island and the South Island of:
e: Cook Strait separates the North Island and the South Island of New Zealand, connecting the Tasman Sea with the South Pacific Ocean.

q: The Torres Strait lies between northern Australia and the island of:
e: The Torres Strait lies between Cape York in northern Australia and the island of New Guinea to its north.

q: The Dardanelles strait connects the Aegean Sea with the:
e: The Dardanelles strait connects the Aegean Sea with the Sea of Marmara, and onwards through the Bosporus to the Black Sea.

q: The Atacama Desert, regarded as the driest non-polar desert of the world, lies mainly in the northern part of:
e: The Atacama Desert, regarded as the driest non-polar desert in the world, lies mainly in northern Chile along the Pacific coast.

q: The largest part of the Kalahari Desert lies in the country of:
e: The largest part of the Kalahari Desert lies in Botswana, covering much of that country, with extensions into Namibia and South Africa.

q: The Grand Canyon in the United States was carved out over millions of years by the river:
e: The Grand Canyon in the United States was carved over millions of years by the Colorado River flowing through northern Arizona.

q: The Three Gorges Dam, one of the largest power stations of the world, has been built in China on the river:
e: The Three Gorges Dam, among the largest power stations in the world, has been built in China on the Yangtze River.

q: The ancient land of Mesopotamia, home to some of the earliest civilisations, lay between the rivers:
e: Mesopotamia, the land between the rivers, lay between the Tigris and the Euphrates in present-day Iraq and hosted early civilisations like Sumer and Babylon.

q: The Iguazu Falls, among the largest waterfall systems of the world, lie on the border between:
e: The Iguazu Falls, among the largest waterfall systems in the world, lie on the Iguazu River on the border between Argentina and Brazil.

q: The Chambal River originates in the Janapav Hills near Mhow in the State of:
e: The Chambal River originates in the Janapav Hills near Mhow in Madhya Pradesh, in the Vindhya range, and later joins the Yamuna.

q: The Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, was named after the astronomer:
e: The Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, was named after Edwin Hubble, the astronomer known for evidence of the expanding universe.

q: Members of the Railway Board, other than the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, hold the ex-officio status of ____ to the Government of India.
e: Members of the Railway Board other than the Chairman and CEO hold the ex-officio status of Secretary to the Government of India, while the Chairman and CEO is Principal Secretary.

q: The Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA) has been set up primarily for:

options.A: Commercial development of vacant railway land and air space

e: The Rail Land Development Authority has been set up primarily for commercial development of vacant railway land and air space for revenue generation.

q: The campus of the National Academy of Indian Railways (NAIR) at Vadodara is housed in the historic building known as:
e: The campus of the National Academy of Indian Railways at Vadodara is housed in the historic Pratap Vilas Palace.

q: The Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor, being implemented by DFCCIL from Ludhiana to Dankuni, has a total route length of about:
e: The Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor implemented by DFCCIL from Ludhiana to Dankuni, including its sections, has a total route length of about 1,856 km as sanctioned.

q: The Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) was granted the 'Navratna' status by the Government of India in the year:
e: IRCTC was granted Navratna status by the Government of India in 2025, along with IRFC, giving it greater financial and operational autonomy.

q: The Konkan Railway, built and operated by the Konkan Railway Corporation Limited between Roha and Thokur, has a route length of about:
e: The Konkan Railway, built and operated by KRCL between Roha and Thokur, has a route length of about 741 km along the west coast.

q: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor, being executed by NHSRCL, has a total length of about:
e: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor executed by NHSRCL has a total length of about 508 km between the two cities.

q: For the vacancy cycle 2025-26, the centralised Computer Based Test for the AFA LDCE of the Accounts Department is being conducted by the:

options.A: National Academy of Indian Railways, Vadodara

e: For the vacancy cycle 2025-26, the centralised Computer Based Test for the AFA LDCE of the Accounts Department is being conducted by the Railway Recruitment Board, Ajmer.

q: The Commissioner of Railway Safety (CRS), who inquires into serious railway accidents, functions under the administrative control of the:

options.D: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways

e: The Commissioner of Railway Safety, who inquires into serious railway accidents, functions under the administrative control of the Ministry of Civil Aviation, keeping it independent of Railways.

q: The Railway Convention Committee of Parliament is primarily concerned with reviewing and fixing the:

options.C: Rate of dividend payable by the Railways to the general revenues

e: The Railway Convention Committee of Parliament is primarily concerned with reviewing and fixing the rate of dividend payable by the Railways to the general revenues.

q: The National Railway Users' Consultative Council (NRUCC), the apex consultative body of railway users, is chaired by the:

options.B: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Railway Board

e: The National Railway Users Consultative Council, the apex consultative body of railway users, is chaired by the Minister of Railways.

q: The Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs) function under the overall guidance and coordination of the:
e: The Railway Recruitment Boards function under the overall guidance and coordination of the Railway Recruitment Control Board in the Ministry of Railways.

q: Who became the first Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the restructured Railway Board in September 2020?
e: Vinod Kumar Yadav became the first Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the restructured Railway Board in September 2020, after serving as Chairman, Railway Board.

q: The Railway Board was set up under the Indian Railway Board Act enacted in the year:
e: The Railway Board was set up under the Indian Railway Board Act enacted in 1905, separating railway administration from the Public Works Department.

q: The headquarters of the Northeast Frontier Railway is located at:
e: The headquarters of the Northeast Frontier Railway is located at Maligaon in Guwahati, Assam.

q: The Integral Coach Factory (ICF) at Chennai was set up with technical collaboration from:
e: The Integral Coach Factory at Chennai was set up with technical collaboration from Switzerland, based on the Swiss Schlieren design of light-weight coaches.

q: 'Rail Sadan' at Bhubaneswar is the headquarters building of the:
e: Rail Sadan at Bhubaneswar is the headquarters building of the East Coast Railway zone.

q: The North Eastern Railway, with headquarters at Gorakhpur, was formed in the year:
e: The North Eastern Railway, with headquarters at Gorakhpur, was formed in 1952 by merging the Oudh and Tirhut Railway with other systems.

q: The Diesel Loco Shed at Erode functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Diesel Loco Shed at Erode is in Tamil Nadu and functions under Southern Railway, whose territory covers that area.

q: The Electric Loco Shed at Ludhiana functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Electric Loco Shed at Ludhiana is in Punjab and functions under Northern Railway, the zone covering Ludhiana.
